Recruitment Tracks and Departments
Track
Definition
Departments for Admission
Korean Language Track
This is the admission process that verifies the 'Korean language proficiency' of applicants at the time of admission, and most of the classes are conducted in Korean.
Please refer to the admission guidelines for more details
English Track
？This is the admission process that assesses the 'English proficiency' of applicants at the time of admission, and most of the classes are conducted in English.
Please refer to the admission guidelines for more details.
Chinese Track
This is the admission process that assesses the 'Chinese proficiency' of applicants at the time of admission, and most of the classes are conducted in Chinese.
International Law Department
The recruitment departments and the availability of Korean/English tracks may change each semester, so please refer to the recruitment guidelines.

Nationality Criteria
Foreign Students with Both Parents Being Foreign Nationals
※ Dual Citizens and Stateless Individuals are Not Recognized as Foreign Nationals
eligibility criteria based on one's educational background
Master's Degree
1. Graduates or Prospective Graduates of 4-year Universities in Korea or Abroad
2. Individuals Recognized as Having Equivalent or Higher Qualifications Under Other Laws
Doctoral Degree
1. Individuals who have obtained or are expected to obtain a master's degree from domestic or foreign graduate schools
2. Individuals recognized as having equivalent or higher qualifications under other laws
Integrated Master's and Doctoral Program Type 1
Equivalent to the Master's Degree Program
Integrated Master's and Doctoral Program Type 2
1. Individuals who are currently in their 2nd semester or beyond of the master's program at our university (students in the 3rd or 4th semester)
2. Those whose major field in the master's program matches the major field they are applying for in the integrated program
※ Taking a leave of absence before entering the integrated program is not allowed (if a leave of absence is taken, the acceptance will be canceled).
※ Applications from students on leave of absence or graduates are not accepted."

※ Language proficiency scores are only accepted if obtained within 2 years from the application date
※ However, the following applicants may be exempt from submitting language proficiency scores
Division
Details
Applicants for the English Track who are from countries where English is the native language (South Africa, New Zealand, the United States, Ireland, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia) and have completed secondary education or higher education (university-level courses)
Applicants who do not possess language proficiency test scores may be exempt from submitting a score and will be evaluated through an interview for final admission. In this case, they must submit proof of completing their secondary or higher education in English. (Applicants with language proficiency scores should submit their language test scores.)
Applicants for science and engineering, arts and physical education, and medicine
Applicants without language proficiency scores may be exempt from submitting their scores and will be evaluated through an interview. (Applicants with language proficiency scores should submit their language proficiency test scores.)
